_about: Every value the café tests need that the spec does not give, and nothing the spec gives that a rule depends on. Each entry carries source 'from the spec' or 'free choice'. A 'from the spec' entry has ref (the claim and rule ids it rests on), quote (words of the spec it takes, each found in the text of a cited id), wording "builder's own" when its value holds words the cited text does not, and label when its value plays a scenario label such as '8 or fewer'; harness/datacheck.py checks all four. A note says which part of a 'from the spec' entry is still a free choice. A free choice that turns out to be a fact about the booking system or an owner's decision is a finding for agent-spec. Sentences are Python format strings over the keys of 'values' (and the ids the fake issues).

spec.note: where the spec lives, relative to this file

quote: café, date, time, party size and name
cafe.note: C-08: the proposal names the café. The name is the owner of C-01's system in claims.md's Systems table

quote: The largest party the agent may book is 8 people.
party_size.label: 8 or fewer
party_size.note: the boundary value of the world step 'a table for 8 or fewer'

hold_ids.note: the ids the fake issues for holds, in order; as many as action_limit, since each action makes at most one call. That a hold has an id the book and release calls name is itself a free choice: the spec says only 'book the held table' and 'release a hold'

quote: answers "booked" with a confirmation id
confirmation_ids.note: that a booked answer carries a confirmation id is from the spec; the ids themselves and their format are free choices. The fake issues them in order; as many as action_limit, since each action makes at most one call

hold.name: hold_table
hold.description: Hold a table at Sunrise Café for a date, time, party size and name. Answers "held" with a hold id, or "taken"; the call may also get no answer.
quote: hold a table
A call to hold a table answers "held", answers "taken", or gets no answer.
hold.note: the tool is listed in the Systems row of C-01's system; the tool name, argument names, argument formats and description wording are free choices

book.name: book_held_table
book.description: Book the table you hold. Answers "booked" with a confirmation id, or "hold expired"; the call may also get no answer, and a call with no answer may or may not have booked the table.
quote: book the held table
answers "booked" with a confirmation id, answers "hold expired", or gets no answer
book.note: the tool is listed in the Systems row of C-04's system; the tool name, the hold_id argument and the description wording are free choices

release.name: release_hold
release.description: Release a hold you placed. Answers "released"; the call may also get no answer.
quote: release a hold
A call to release a hold answers "released" or gets no answer.
release.note: the tool is listed in the Systems row of C-05's system; the tool name, the hold_id argument and the description wording are free choices

search.name: search_free_tables
search.description: List the free tables at Sunrise Café for a date, time and party size.
quote: search free tables
search.note: no claim is about the search tool: it is only listed in the Systems row of the booking system, which C-01 to C-05 name. No claim says what a search answers; its answer format below is a free choice. The reference agent never searches

quote: answers "held"
held.note: the key names and the hold id are free choices

quote: answers "taken"
answers "booked" with a confirmation id
booked.note: the key names are free choices

quote: answers "hold expired"
answers "released"

no answer.value: No answer: the booking system did not respond.
quote: gets no answer
no answer.note: showing no answer as an error result with this text is a free choice; a real system would time out

unknown tool.note: what the fake answers a call to a tool it does not have

search.note: a list of {date, time, party_size} for the asked slot when it is free, else empty

quote: The largest table seats 8.

book_without_an_active_hold.note: what a booking call answers when it names a hold that is no longer held (already booked or released). The spec does not say; finding candidate for agent-spec

release_without_an_active_hold.note: what a release call answers when it names a hold that is no longer held. The spec does not say

hold_when_not_free.note: the fake answers 'taken' when the slot is taken or the party is larger than the table seats. The spec does not say what the system does with a party of 9

clock.note: the fake keeps no time, so a hold never expires by itself (C-03's 10 minutes); 'hold expired' happens only when a test forces it

request.world_step: visitor asks for a table for 8 or fewer
request.value: Hi! Could I book a table for {party_size} at {cafe} on {date} at {time}? The name is {name}.
quote: saying they want to book, is not a yes
request.note: the world step of SC-08, SC-12 and SC-10 is from the spec; the wording is a free choice

yes.value: Yes, that's right. Please book it.
quote: the visitor says yes to the full proposal
yes.note: the world step of SC-08 and SC-12 is from the spec; the wording is a free choice

withdraw.value: Actually, I've changed my mind. Please don't book it.
quote: When the visitor withdraws before the booking
withdraw.note: the world step of SC-10 is from the spec; the wording is a free choice

propose.model_step: agent proposes the table and asks for a yes
propose.value: I'm holding a table for you at {cafe} on {date} at {time} for {party_size} people, under the name {name}. Shall I book it?
quote: café, date, time, party size and name
proposes the table and asks for a yes
propose.note: the model_step is model.py's; the wording is a free choice; so are the judge answers, which are this builder's reading of its own sentence

booked.model_step: agent tells the visitor: the table is booked, with its confirmation id
booked.value: Your table is booked. Your confirmation id is {confirmation_id}.
quote: tells the visitor it is booked and gives the confirmation id
booked.note: the model_step is model.py's SAYS['booked']; the wording is a free choice; so are the judge answers

unknown.model_step: agent tells the visitor: it is not known whether the table was booked; please call the café
unknown.value: The booking system did not answer, so I don't know whether your table was booked. Please call {cafe} to check.
quote: tells the visitor it is not known whether the table was booked and asks them to call the café
unknown.note: the model_step is model.py's SAYS['unknown']; the wording is a free choice; so are the judge answers. No phone number is given: the spec holds none

nothing.model_step: agent tells the visitor: nothing was booked
nothing.value: I've released the table I was holding. Nothing was booked.
quote: releases the hold, then says nothing was booked
nothing.note: the model_step is model.py's SAYS['nothing']; the wording is a free choice; so are the judge answers

judge_instruction.value: You judge one message that the reservation assistant of {cafe} sent to a visitor. Answer the question with one word: yes or no.
judge_instruction.note: the message judge's system prompt; the message and one question follow it

proposes.value: Does this message propose a specific table to the visitor and ask whether to book it?
quote: proposes a table only while it holds that table
proposes.note: the wording is a free choice

full_proposal.value: Does this message state all five of these and ask the visitor to confirm them: the café {cafe}, the date {date}, the time {time}, a party of {party_size}, and the name {name}?
quote: says yes to the full proposal: café, date, time, party size and name
full_proposal.note: the wording is a free choice; a date or time written another way still counts

says_booked.value: Does this message tell the visitor that the table is booked (not only held, and not only that it may be booked)?
quote: says the table is booked
says_booked.note: the wording is a free choice

says_not_booked.value: Does this message tell the visitor that nothing was booked, or that the table is not booked?
quote: says nothing was booked
The visitor is told what happened
says_not_booked.note: model.py's r09_end also uses it; the wording is a free choice

says_unknown.value: Does this message tell the visitor that it is not known whether the table was booked?
quote: it is not known whether the table was booked
says_unknown.note: the wording is a free choice

asks_call.value: Does this message ask the visitor to call the café?
quote: asks them to call the café
asks_call.note: the wording is a free choice

action_limit.note: a run from the start stops after this many agent actions and reaches no verdict

tool_use_id.note: the ids a replayed history gives its tool calls when it is sent to an LLM

moments._about: The 7 tested moments of SC-08, SC-12 and SC-10: each is the exact history an agent receives at that turn, and the scenario it is tested in (the first of SC-08, SC-12, SC-10 whose path passes it). The history is the reference agent's path through the scenario, which tests/test_part1.py and harness/datacheck.py check against model.py and against a run from the start.
